title: Quasi-regular sequences with flat quotient survive arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $R\to A$ and $R\to R'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Let $b\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$, and $C=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume that $C$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_J(A),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes r)(a_1\otimes r_1)=aa_1\otimes rr_1$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and put $f'_j=f_j\otimes1$, $J'=(f'_1,\ldots,f'_b)$, and $C'=A'/J'$. Then the canonical graded $C'$-algebra homomorphism
$$C'[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{J'}(A'),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f'_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism. No flatness of $R\to R'$, flatness of $R\to A$, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, part (1); quasi-regularity is the displayed isomorphism of algebra.tex Tag 061P.

proof.text: Put C=A/J. The polynomial ring C[T] is free over C, hence flat over C, and is flat over R by transitivity [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. Regard the assumed graded polynomial bijection as an R-linear equivalence: the quotient-algebra scalar action agrees with the natural action on each representative. Flatness passes across the equivalence. Each homogeneous summand of the associated graded ring is a direct summand and hence flat (Module.Flat.directSum_iff). This proves flatness of every J^n/J^(n+1) without enumerating the finite degree-n monomials.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Every A/J^m is R-flat. For m=0 the quotient is zero; for m=1 this is the hypothesis. For n>=1 use the exact sequence 0 -> J^n/J^(n+1) -> A/J^(n+1) -> A/J^n -> 0. The first map takes the class of x to the class of its value; its kernel is zero, and a class dies under the last map precisely when its representative belongs to J^n. Extensions of flat modules are flat: tensor an arbitrary injection with this sequence, use right exactness and flat-quotient tensor injectivity, and chase an element using flatness of the outer terms. This chase is already proved as Module.Flat.of_exact_of_flat_of_flat in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.Equalizer.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Let B=A tensor_R R' and K=(f_j tensor 1). Extension sends J to K and J^n to K^n. The image of u_n:J^n tensor R' -> B is K^n (Ideal.map_includeLeft_eq and Ideal.map_pow); the tensor inclusion is injective because A/J^n is R-flat, by lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective. The maps u_(n+1) and u_n commute with the inclusion of ideal powers, as is checked on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: For each monomial index d compose J^n -> J^n/J^(n+1) -> gr_J(A) with the inverse of the assumed polynomial bijection and with coefficient projection. This gives an R-linear map c_d:J^n -> C which kills J^(n+1). If |e|=n, then c_d(a*f^e) is [a] for e=d and zero otherwise, since the original polynomial map sends [a]*T^e to the class of a*f^e in degree n. All maps here are explicitly constructed from the given bijection.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Take a homogeneous degree-n polynomial p over B whose evaluation lies in K^(n+1). Its finite monomial expansion lifts to x=sum_e (multiplication by f^e tensor R')(coefficient_e(p)) in J^n tensor R'. The evaluation also lifts to y in J^(n+1) tensor R'. Since u_n is injective, x equals the inclusion of y. Applying c_d tensor R' makes the latter zero and makes the former the image of coefficient_d(p) under (A -> C) tensor R', by the delta formula of the preceding step. Thus this tensor image is zero. The canonical quotient tensor equivalence C tensor R' = B/K, sending [a] tensor s to [a tensor s], now gives coefficient_d(p) in K. Its formula is checked on pure tensors (Algebra.TensorProduct.quotientTensorEquiv_apply_tmul).

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: The resulting homogeneous relation criterion implies bijectivity of the canonical polynomial map over B/K. For injectivity, lift coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial over B/K to B with the same support. Vanishing of its graded image means that its evaluation belongs to the next ideal power. The criterion says every lifted coefficient belongs to K, hence the original homogeneous polynomial is zero. Apply this to each homogeneous component. For surjectivity, each representative in K^n is the evaluation of a homogeneous degree-n polynomial by Ideal.mem_span_pow_iff_exists_isHomogeneous; reduce coefficients modulo K and sum the finitely many graded components. This proves the given canonical algebra map bijective, also when b=0 or the quotient ring is zero.
